module_summary: Host-testable pure-C memory card image code used by the dashboard card tool (src/dash_card_tool.c), MMCE backup fingerprinting (src/mmce_backup.c) and save versions (src/mmce_save_versions.c). mc_card_view.c reads PS2 card images (.mcd/.bin and ECC .ps2) through a read callback: superblock validation, bounded FAT/chain walks, save listing, free-cluster count and a SHA-256 index fingerprint. mc_card_write.c adds crash-ordered save copy/delete with read-back, .psu import/export, blank card formatting and Game ID helpers. mc_ps1_card.c handles 128 KB PS1 card images and single-save files (.mcs/.psv/.psx/raw) in memory; mc_save_export.c writes signed .psv, .psx, stored .zip and the PS1 card containers (.gme/.vgs/.vmp/.mcx) using Mbed TLS AES/HMAC. mc_save_formats.h only declares the readers implemented in src/mc_save_formats.c (another unit). Input validation is thorough: every walk is bounded and every parsed length is checked; no overflow or reachable crash was found.

reusable_helpers.what: builds the PS3 .PSV file name from a save name (12 chars then hex)

reusable_helpers.what: AES-128 ECB single block or CBC in place over Mbed TLS

findings.title: Imported save is read back twice: mcCardWriteSave verifies, then ctPutSave reopens and reads the whole save again
findings.problem: mcCardWriteSave step 6 already reopens the view (fresh mcViewOpen), reads the whole save into a second McSaveData and compares it with sameSave. ctPutSave then closes, reopens the image read-only and does the same full mcCardReadSave + mcCardSameSave again. Every single-save import (5 ctPutSave callers) therefore reads, mallocs and compares the full save data twice, synchronously on the UI thread under the loading overlay.
findings.fix: Delete the second read-back in ctPutSave (dash_card_tool.c:415-426) and return the mcCardWriteSave result once ctClose succeeded. Keep the verify inside mcCardWriteSave, which the batch paths (dash_card_tool.c:1088 and 1170) rely on.
findings.benefit: One full read of the save (all its data clusters through fileXio) plus one full-size malloc/compare removed per import; ~11 lines removed (INFERRED: count of dash_card_tool.c:415-426).
findings.evidence: Read mc_card_write.c:653-662 (reopen, mcCardReadSave, sameSave) and dash_card_tool.c:392-427 (ctPutSave: mcCardWriteSave at 408, ctClose, ctOpen, mcCardReadSave, mcCardSameSave at 417-425). grep ctPutSave: callers at dash_card_tool.c:523, 937, 1892, 2114, 2500. grep dashWorker in dash_card_tool.c: no matches, so these run on the UI thread (dashLoadingStatus, dash_ui.c:1406). INFERRED part: the post-close read catches no failure the in-function read misses, because both read through fileXio on the same device and ctClose's return is already checked at 409-413.

findings.title: mcCardWriteSave writes save data one 1 KB cluster per lseek+write RPC pair, copying each through a bounce buffer
findings.problem: Each data cluster is memset+memcpy'd into buf and written with its own writeAt call; the card tool's write callback ctWrite does genLseek (fileXioLseek64) plus genWrite (fileXioWrite) per call. A 1 MB save costs 1024 writes = 2048 EE-to-IOP RPCs on the UI thread. writerAlloc hands out the lowest free clusters in ascending order (mc_card_write.c:374-386), so a chain is usually a few runs of consecutive clusters that could each be one write.
findings.fix: In step 1, write each run of consecutive chain clusters with one writeAt straight from fl->data (no memset/memcpy), and send only the final partial cluster through buf with its zero padding.
findings.justification: Adds about 4 lines to the write loop. The concrete problem is per-cluster RPC pairs and a 1 KB bounce copy for every cluster of every imported save; grouping consecutive clusters is the smallest change that cuts the call count by the run length without a new buffer or cache.
findings.benefit: Write calls per save drop from one per KB to one per contiguous run (often 1-3 per file); removes the per-cluster memcpy. Time saved INFERRED, not measured (roughly 2 RPCs per KB of save data).
findings.evidence: Read mc_card_write.c:408-416 (writeAt/writeCluster, 1024-byte writes), 569-590 (per-cluster memset, memcpy, writeCluster), 374-386 (writerAlloc scans upward from w->scan). dash_card_tool.c:96-117 ctWrite: genLseek then genWrite loop per call, no write cache. filer_fileops.c:690 genLseek -> fileXioLseek64, :747 genWrite -> fileXioWrite. Callers mcCardWriteSave at dash_card_tool.c:408, 1088, 1170 run on the UI thread (no dashWorker use in that file). Timing per RPC not measured.

findings.title: mcViewListSaves and describeSave re-walk the directory chain from its first cluster for every entry (quadratic)
findings.problem: Both loops call dirEntry(v, first, i), which uses chainRead from the first cluster, so entry i costs i/2 chainNext FAT lookups plus one full cluster read; a root of L entries costs about L*L/4 FAT lookups and L cluster reads instead of L/2. The file already has walkDir (lines 383-409), written for exactly this ('instead of re-walking the chain per entry'), used by the fingerprint and rootFind but not by the listing, which the card tool runs on the UI thread after every open and operation.
findings.fix: Drive the root loop of mcViewListSaves and the loop of describeSave with walkDir callbacks, as rootFind (mc_card_write.c:139-151) does.
findings.benefit: INFERRED: root of 600 entries (large 64 MB card) ~90,000 cached FAT lookups and 600 cluster reads become ~300 of each; on typical 8 MB cards (under ~150 entries) the gain is milliseconds. About the same line count.
findings.evidence: Read mc_card_view.c:121-156 chainRead (skip = offset/1024 chainNext steps from 'first'), 165-178 dirEntry (chainRead at i*512), 288-319 describeSave and 321-360 mcViewListSaves (dirEntry per i), 381-409 walkDir comment and code. grep mcViewListSaves: UI-thread callers dash_card_tool.c:451, 1005, 1102, 1180, 1231, 1486, 1566, 1745; mmce_save_versions.c:408, 411. Arithmetic: sum over i<L of i/2 = L*L/4.
